name: Long Put Calendar Spread
summary: Sell a near-term put and buy a longer-dated put at the same strike; the put mirror of the call calendar, used when the pin level is at or below spot or when puts are the more liquid side.

legs.strike_rule: ATM by delta: |delta| 0.45-0.55 neutral; 0.25-0.35 OTM put for a bearish directional calendar. Strike within 1.0 x ATR(14) of spot.

max_profit: No closed form. Approximately the back-month put's theoretical value at front expiry with spot at the strike, minus the debit; typically 20-40% of the debit.
max_loss: The net debit paid, if the underlying finishes far from the strike in either direction by front expiry.
breakevens: Two, bracketing the strike; solve numerically at front expiry with back-month IV. Roughly strike +/- (1.0 to 1.3) x debit in underlying points.

greeks.delta: ~0 at ATM (+/-0.05); moves to +/-0.15 as spot drifts off the strike
greeks.theta: positive, ~+$3 to +$8/day per unit at 30/60 on a $100 name

when_to_use: Same regime as the call calendar: IV rank < 30, term structure flat-to-backwardated. Prefer the put calendar when the pin strike is below spot, when the put side of the chain is tighter, or when the underlying pays a dividend inside the front cycle (short puts have no dividend-driven early-assignment risk; short calls do). On high-dividend ETFs the put calendar is structurally safer than the call calendar.
entry_rules: Front 21-35 DTE, back 45-70 DTE, gap 21-35 days.
Strike by delta: neutral front |delta| 0.45-0.55; directional 0.25-0.35. Within 1.0 ATR(14) of spot.
Net debit <= $2.50/unit on sub-$150 underlyings; total debit <= 2% of equity.
No earnings between now and front expiry unless running the earnings playbook.
LEVEL 3 OK: long back-month put at the same strike and later expiry covers the short front put. Single mleg order; if rejected, fill the LONG leg first.
management_rules: Profit target +25% of debit; acceptable range 25-50%.
Directional stop: |spot - strike| > 1.0 x front-month ATM straddle price at entry.
If |net delta| > 0.30 per unit, close or recenter.
Roll the short put out one expiry when front DTE <= 7 and short |delta| <= 0.60, for a credit only.
Max 4 units per underlying; calendars in aggregate <= 10% of equity.
exit_rules: Close or roll the short put by 14:30 ET on its expiration day, unconditionally.
Close the whole spread no later than 2 trading days before front expiry if not rolling.
Close the short put immediately if extrinsic <= $0.05/share OR short |delta| >= 0.90.
Deep-ITM short puts on hard-to-borrow or high-interest-rate names get exercised early for the interest - close any short put whose extrinsic is below $0.10 regardless of DTE.
If the long put marks below $0.10, close both legs.
assignment_risk: Only the short front-month put. Assignment delivers 100 LONG shares per contract (a cash/buying-power event, not a short-stock event) hedged by a long back-month put. Early exercise of short puts is driven by interest carry on deep-ITM puts, not dividends. If assigned, flatten the shares within one session and re-evaluate the long put.
buying_power: Net debit only; no additional maintenance. Assignment consumes buying power equal to strike x 100 until the shares are sold.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 250 per leg, volume >= 50, back-month quoted spread <= $0.25. Underlying ADV >= 2M shares.
common_mistakes: Treating the put calendar as bearish - it is not, it is neutral around the strike; buying it into high IV rank; forgetting that a deep-ITM short put can be exercised for interest; choosing a strike far below spot for 'safety' and ending up with a structure that only pays if the market crashes precisely to that level.
zero_dte_notes: Same as the call calendar: a 0DTE front leg belongs to the day-calendar playbook only.
family: Calendar and diagonal spreads (time spreads): same-strike calendars, different-strike diagonals, double/triple calendars, double diagonals, PMCC and its put mirror, LEAPS diagonals, calendarized straddles/butterflies, ratio time spreads, and the reverse (short) time spreads
